features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education the applicant presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience only, with no advanced degree presented.
Master's degree in computer science or a related field is presented.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related field is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct design or ownership experience with agent-based systems, including guardrails, supervision, and control boundaries.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as shown through concrete engineering improvements or problem solving.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has shipped AI systems in production and understands the reliability, evaluation, and guardrail work they require.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers through secure defaults, usable tooling, and reduced friction rather than policing or compliance.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates its claims with specific mechanisms, examples, quantities, or named systems rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter establishes Go as a central professional language for relevant backend work.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or only incidentally named.
Go is mentioned as one language used, but without clear depth or centrality.
Go is presented as a regular production language used for meaningful work.
Go is clearly framed as a primary language, daily driver, or principal tool for shipped systems.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures whether the letter explains the results or practical effects of the applicant's work rather than only naming activities or responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a connected story or career arc that coherently links past experience, motivation, and fit for the role.

levels.descriptor: Reads as a disconnected inventory of facts or a compliance-style form letter.
Has some stated motivation, but the link from prior work to this role is thin or mechanical.
Presents a coherent progression from prior experience to the target role.
Tells a memorable, well-shaped story that makes the move into this role feel natural, intentional, and earned.

features.name: Narrative voice
features.description: Captures whether the letter has a distinctive, memorable, and purposeful voice or framing rather than sounding generic or templated.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, list-like, or heavily templated prose.
Is competent and readable, but largely generic in voice.
Has a noticeable hook, framing device, or coherent personal story.
Has a strong, memorable voice that reinforces fit without sacrificing substance.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented or adversarial security practice, especially through capture-the-flag participation or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public or upstream software through contribution, patching, maintenance, or care for external users and communities.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and seriousness of self-directed engineering projects outside formal work responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational or central infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production engineering experience
features.description: Captures the depth of real professional software delivery experience through tenure, shipped services, production ownership, and operational responsibility.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how substantial, central, and production-grade the applicant's Python experience appears.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention Python, or only name-checks it without substance.
Uses Python mainly for light scripting or simple tooling.
Shows substantial Python use across services, automation, or internal systems.
Presents Python as a mature production language, with responsibility for important services or clearly engineered tooling.

features.name: Reliability and rigor mindset
features.description: Captures emphasis on maintainability, correctness, failure handling, and disciplined engineering standards for long-lived systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows little attention to maintainability or resilience.
Uses generic reliability language without much depth.
Shows a clear maintainer or resilience-oriented framing.
Backs a reliability mindset with concrete attention to failure cases, inherited systems, or stewardship.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter targets this exact role and maps the applicant's background to the job's stated responsibilities or requirements.

levels.descriptor: Motivation is generic and mostly repeats the company, title, or desire to apply.
The letter links interest to security or scale, but the reason remains broad.
The letter gives clear role-specific motivation tied to security automation, vulnerability handling, or the team's mandate.
The letter opens with a memorable thesis about the problem space and repeatedly connects that thesis to the applicant's background.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience reviewing systems for security issues through methods like threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands the role's core problem as scaling security work through automation, tooling, and workflow design.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the presence, rigor, and relevance of formal external security certifications or credentialing.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a broader values-driven view of what security engineering is for and why the applicant is drawn to it.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Captures direct experience automating vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface-level professionalism of the letter through proofreading, spelling, grammar, and sentence-level execution.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly belong to one recurring evaluative construct in this set.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.
